# The spacetime Penrose inequality with charge and original-data rigidity

{
  "abstract_verbatim": "Under the stated energy, decay, and trapping hypotheses, we prove the sharp charged spacetime Penrose upper-area inequality for one-ended three-dimensional initial data with source-free electric and magnetic fields. The theorem allows arbitrary second fundamental form, nonzero ADM momentum, and disconnected boundary. Writing <i>m</i> for invariant ADM mass, <i>Q</i> for total charge magnitude, and <i>r</i><sub><i>A</i></sub> for the minimum-enclosing-area radius, the bound is <i>m</i> ≥ <i>Q</i> and $`r_A\\le m+\\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}`$. The polynomial mass bound $`m\\ge(r_A+Q^2/r_A)/2`$ is asserted only when $`r_A\\gt Q`$. When <i>m</i> &gt; <i>Q</i>, equality under the stated connected, outermost, outer-area-minimizing future-horizon hypotheses identifies the original data as a smooth spacelike slice of dyonic Reissner–Nordström, including smooth attachment at the future horizon.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> Under the stated energy, decay, and trapping hypotheses, we prove the sharp charged spacetime Penrose upper-area inequality for one-ended three-dimensional initial data with source-free electric and magnetic fields. The theorem allows arbitrary second fundamental form, nonzero ADM momentum, and disconnected boundary. Writing <i>m</i> for invariant ADM mass, <i>Q</i> for total charge magnitude, and <i>r</i><sub><i>A</i></sub> for the minimum-enclosing-area radius, the bound is <i>m</i> ≥ <i>Q</i> and $`r_A\le m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}`$. The polynomial mass bound $`m\ge(r_A+Q^2/r_A)/2`$ is asserted only when $`r_A\gt Q`$. When <i>m</i> &gt; <i>Q</i>, equality under the stated connected, outermost, outer-area-minimizing future-horizon hypotheses identifies the original data as a smooth spacelike slice of dyonic Reissner–Nordström, including smooth attachment at the future horizon.

- **claim-charged-upper-area** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-numerical)): Let the data satisfy Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a>, and suppose $\theta_+\le0$ on every component of $S$. Then $E>\|P\|$, the invariant ADM mass $m=\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|^2}$ is positive, and $$\label{eq:main-inequality} E\ge\sqrt{\|P\|^2+Q^2},\qquad m\ge Q,\qquad r_A\le m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}.$$ The same conclusion holds if, on each boundary component, one fixes either the condition $H+\operatorname{tr}_S K\le0$ or the condition $H-\operatorname{tr}_S K\le0$.
  - Explanation: The charged energy and enclosing-radius bounds hold for the original exterior, and its ADM vector is future timelike. Boundary signs may be chosen separately by component.
- **claim-original-data-rigidity** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-rigidity)): Assume the connected horizon class and $m>Q$. If $$\label{eq:main-equality} \sqrt{\frac{A}{4\pi}}=m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2},$$ then the entire original quadruple $(g,K,\mathcal E,\mathcal B)$, including its boundary, is induced by a global smooth orientation-preserving spacelike embedding into the regular future-horizon extension of one exterior of dyonic Reissner–Nordström with parameters $(m,Q_E,Q_B)$.* *The image lies in the domain of outer communication together with its corresponding future horizon. The boundary is a full smooth horizon cross-section or the bifurcation sphere, and the chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The embedding, its future unit normal and the induced electromagnetic fields extend smoothly to $S$. The non-electromagnetic matter densities vanish throughout the exterior.
  - Explanation: Saturation in the connected nondegenerate horizon class identifies all original tensors through a smooth spacelike embedding into dyonic Reissner–Nordström, including the horizon boundary.
- **claim-converse-sharpness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-converse)): Let $M>\sqrt{q_E^2+q_B^2}$, and put $R_+=M+\sqrt{M^2-q_E^2-q_B^2}$. Every smooth spacelike exterior hypersurface of dyonic Reissner–Nordström with these parameters whose induced data satisfy Definitions <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a> and <a href="#def:rigidity-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:rigidity-class">4</a>, whose boundary is a full cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or its bifurcation sphere, and whose actual invariant ADM mass and outward charge fluxes are $M,q_E,q_B$, satisfies $$a_g(S)=\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(S)=4\pi R_+^2$$ and attains equality in Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical">3</a>. For every such parameter triple there are admissible static examples, examples with $K\not\equiv0$, and examples with nonzero ADM momentum.
  - Explanation: Admissible Reissner–Nordström exterior slices with the prescribed actual mass and fluxes attain equality. Static, non-time-symmetric and boosted examples exist.
- **claim-full-cut-flux** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-flux)): If $\beta$ is a smooth closed two-form on $\Omega$, smooth up to $S$, then for every full enclosing cut $\Gamma$ and every sufficiently distant coordinate sphere $S_r$, $$\label{ct:flux-identity} \int_\Gamma\beta=\int_{S_r}\beta=\int_S\beta.$$ No extension of $\beta$ across $S$ is required.
  - Explanation: Closed flux forms have the same integral on the full intrinsic boundary, every full enclosure and a distant sphere. Boundary contact does not remove a flux contribution.
- **claim-positive-enclosing-area** (bound, [source](#stmt-ct-full-cut-positive)): Under the geometric hypotheses of Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a>, $$\label{ct:positive-area} 0<a_g(S)\leq\operatorname{Area}_g(S)<\infty.$$ There is, more precisely, a smooth closed two-form $\beta$ on $\Omega$ with finite positive comass bound $C_\beta$ and $\int_\Gamma\beta=1$ for every full cut. Thus $a_g(S)\geq C_\beta^{-1}$.
  - Explanation: The geometric exterior assumptions alone force a positive finite enclosing-area infimum through a bounded-comass closed form.
- **claim-minimizer-confinement** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-confinement)): There are compact truncations $C_{R_0}\subset\operatorname{int}C_{R_1}$ containing $F$ such that the infimum in Equation <a href="#ct:perimeter-infimum" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ct:perimeter-infimum">[ct:perimeter-infimum]</a> is attained and every bounded minimizer is contained in $C_{R_0}$ up to a null set. The same truncations work for a family with uniform asymptotic bounds $g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_1(r^{-q})$, $q>0$, on a common end. The existence and confinement statements also hold for an arbitrary bounded measurable obstacle in place of $F$.
  - Explanation: Positive end mean curvature confines perimeter minimizers and makes the infimum attainable, uniformly for the stated families of metrics.
- **claim-perimeter-cut-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-perimeter-equivalence)): The auxiliary minimum equals the intrinsic smooth-cut infimum: $$\label{ct:infima-equal} p_g(F)=a_g(S).$$ Every minimizing set has a regular representative with compact embedded $C^{1,1}$ frontier, smooth and minimal away from the obstacle. Thus its frontier is $C^{1,\alpha}$ for every $0<\alpha<1$ and has $W^{2,2}$ local graphs. It has no bounded complementary component. Its exterior is connected to the unique end, and its entire frontier, including contact with $S$, carries its perimeter measure.
  - Explanation: The filled obstacle minimum equals the intrinsic smooth-cut infimum. Its regular frontier retains its whole perimeter, including obstacle contact.
- **claim-minimal-obstacle-regularity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-minimal-obstacle)): If every component of the smooth obstacle boundary is minimal, every minimizing frontier in Proposition <a href="#ct:perimeter-equivalence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ct:perimeter-equivalence">10</a> is smooth and minimal everywhere. If a frontier meets a connected component of the obstacle boundary, it contains that entire component.
  - Explanation: A minimal obstacle permits smooth minimal continuation through contact, and contact with a connected obstacle component forces coincidence with that component.
- **claim-metric-area-continuity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-metric-comparison)): If $g_j\geq c_jg$ on $\Omega$, $c_j\to1$, and $g_j\to g$ uniformly on compact sets, then $a_{g_j}(S)\to a_g(S)$.
  - Explanation: Compact metric convergence and a global lower metric comparison imply convergence of the enclosing infimum.
- **claim-strict-minimizer-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-strict-compactness)): Let smooth metrics $g_j$ converge to $g$ uniformly on compact sets, with common end bounds as in Lemma <a href="#ct:confinement" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ct:confinement">9</a>, and choose their auxiliary extensions to converge uniformly on the filling. If $M_j\in\mathcal M_{g_j}(F)$, a subsequence converges to $M\in\mathcal M_g(F)$ with $$\label{ct:strict-convergence} \mathbf1_{M_j}\longrightarrow\mathbf1_M\quad\text{in }L^1,\qquad P_g(M_j)\longrightarrow P_g(M)=p_g(F).$$ For every continuous function $\Psi$ on the bundle of unoriented two-planes over the common compact truncation, $$\label{ct:plane-measure-continuity} \int_{\partial M_j}\Psi(x,T_x\partial M_j)\,dA_g \longrightarrow\int_{\partial M}\Psi(x,T_x\partial M)\,dA_g.$$ Thus $\mathcal M_g(F)$ is a compact metric space, and the area first-variation functional is continuous on it.
  - Explanation: Minimizers have subsequential strict perimeter convergence, including convergence of continuous tangent-plane integrals and area variation functionals.
- **claim-area-infimum-derivative** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-area-derivative)): Let $g_s$ be a path of smooth exterior metrics with $g_0=g$, common end bounds as in Lemma <a href="#ct:confinement" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="ct:confinement">9</a>, and $$g_s=g+sh+o(\|s\|)\quad\text{in }C^0$$ on a common compact truncation including the filling. For the fixed obstacle $F$ with exterior boundary $B$, set $a(s)=a_{g_s}(B)$. Then $$\label{ct:minimum-derivative} \left.\frac{d}{ds}\right\|_{0+}a(s) =\min_{M\in\mathcal M_g(F)}L_h(M),\qquad L_h(M)=\frac12\int_{\partial M} \operatorname{tr}_{T\partial M}h\,dA_g.$$ Only exterior and boundary values of $h$ enter the integral.
  - Explanation: The right derivative of the enclosing infimum is the minimum first variation over the compact minimizing family, without choosing a differentiable minimizer.
- **claim-compatible-minimizer-planes** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ct-compatible-planes)): For a fixed smooth compact obstacle $F$, the set $$\mathcal Z=\bigcup_{M\in\mathcal M_g(F)}\partial M$$ is compact. At each $x\in\mathcal Z$, all minimizing frontiers through $x$ have the same unoriented tangent plane $T(x)$, and $T$ is continuous on $\mathcal Z$. If $\pi$ is a Borel probability measure on $\mathcal M_g(F)$ and $$\eta(A)=\int_{\mathcal M_g(F)} \operatorname{Area}_g(A\cap\partial M)\,d\pi(M),$$ then, for every continuous function $\Psi$ on the plane bundle, $$\label{ct:averaged-plane} \int_{\mathcal M_g(F)}\int_{\partial M} \Psi(x,T_x\partial M)\,dA_g\,d\pi(M) =\int_{\mathcal Z}\Psi(x,T(x))\,d\eta(x).$$
  - Explanation: All minimizing frontiers through a point share a continuous unoriented tangent plane, so averaging surfaces produces a spatial measure with a single plane above each point.
- **claim-conformal-constraint-identities** (theorem, [source](#stmt-en-conformal)): Let $u>0$, $g'=u^4g$, $K'=u^2K$, and retain $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$. Then $$\label{en:conformal-constraints} \begin{split} u^4\mu'&=\mu-4u^{-1}\Delta_g u,\\ u^2J'&=J+4K(\nabla\log u,\cdot),\\ X_i(g')&=u^{-6}X_i(g),\qquad I_{g'}(u^{-2}Y)=u^{-8}I_g(Y). \end{split}$$ In particular, $$\label{en:conformal-exact} \begin{split} u^4D_{g'}(u^{-2}Y)-D_g(Y) ={}&4u^{-1}\{-\Delta_g u+K(\nabla u,Y)\}\\ &+(1-u^{-4})I_g(Y). \end{split}$$ If $u\geq1$, it follows that $$\label{en:conformal-margin} u^4D_{g'}(u^{-2}Y) \geq D_g(Y)+4u^{-1}(-\Delta_g u-\|K\|_g\|du\|_g).$$ For a fixed oriented surface and either fixed sign $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$, write $\theta_\sigma=H+\sigma\operatorname{tr}_S K$. Then $$\label{en:conformal-expansion} \theta'_\sigma=u^{-2}(\theta_\sigma+4\partial_\nu\log u).$$
  - Explanation: Keeping flux forms fixed gives exact conformal transformation laws for constraints, fields and signed boundary expansions, together with a charged energy margin estimate.
- **claim-asymptotic-lorentz-flux** (theorem, [source](#stmt-en-adm-flux)): Let $G=\eta+h$ be a Lorentzian metric on an exterior region containing the spacelike planes under consideration and the portions of their connecting cylinders at large radius. In background inertial coordinates suppose, uniformly on these regions, $$h=O_2(r^{-q_0}),\qquad q_0>1/2,\qquad \operatorname{Ein}(G)=O(r^{-4}).$$ Use signature $(-+++)$ and the positive second-form convention $K(U,V)=G(\nabla_U n,V)$. If the ADM limits on one plane exist, they exist on every fixed uniformly spacelike plane, and they are the components of the same translation covector $\mathcal C$: $$\label{en:translation-covector} \mathcal C(a)=E a^0+\sum_iP_i a^i.$$ In particular, if $E>\|P\|$ and $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}$, the unit future vector $b=(E/m,-P/m)$ satisfies $\mathcal C(b)=m$.* *The same conclusion applies to a stationary vacuum or electrovacuum end whenever these estimates hold in its stationary coordinates, after a constant linear change making its limiting metric Minkowski. In coordinates adapted to a stationary field with unit timelike limit, suppose the shift has order $O_1(r^{-q_0})$. Then the energy of a rest plane equals that of the spatial orbit metric. This energy is also unchanged by spatial coordinate changes $y=x+\zeta(x)$ with $\zeta=O_2(r^{1-q_1})$, $q_1>1/2$.
  - Explanation: Under the specified spacetime decay, ADM fluxes on fixed spacelike planes represent the same translation covector. Rest energy agrees with orbit-metric energy in the stated stationary regime.
- **claim-strict-conformal-direction** (construction, [source](#stmt-en-strictification)): Suppose $g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$ and $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$, $q>1/2$, on the single end. Fix $0<\delta_0<\min(q,1)$. There are smooth functions $b\geq \|K\|_g$, $a>0$, $w>0$, and $\phi>0$ such that $$\label{en:strict-pde} \begin{gathered} -\Delta_g\phi=b\sqrt{\|d\phi\|_g^2+a^2}+w, \qquad \partial_\nu\phi=-1\quad\hbox{on }S,\\ \phi=O_2(r^{-1}),\qquad b=Cr^{-1-q},\quad a=r^{-2},\quad w=r^{-3-\delta_0} \quad\hbox{far out}. \end{gathered}$$ The gradient flux of $\phi$ has a finite limit at infinity. In particular $u=1+s\phi$, $s>0$, preserves charged DEC and makes it strict, with margin at least $c_s r^{-3-\delta_0}$ on the tail, and makes every weak fixed-sign boundary expansion strictly negative.* *If $K$ is compactly supported and $g-\delta=O_\ell(r^{-1})$ for every $\ell$, one may choose $b$ compactly supported. In that case $-\Delta_g\phi=w$ on the tail and $\phi=O_\ell(r^{-1})$ for every $\ell$. If also $R_g=O_\ell(r^{-4})$, then $R_{(1+s\phi)^4g}=O_\ell(r^{-3-\delta_0})$ for every $\ell$.
  - Explanation: A positive mixed-boundary elliptic solution produces arbitrarily small strictifying conformal changes while preserving fluxes and enforcing strict signed trapping.
- **claim-timelike-endpoint-reduction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-en-timelike-reduction)): Suppose the numerical conclusion of Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical">3</a> has been proved for all data in its class satisfying $E>\|P\|$. Then every datum in the full class satisfies $E>\|P\|$, and the numerical conclusion holds for the full class.
  - Explanation: Once the numerical bound is available for future-timelike data, a positive enclosing-area lower bound and an energy-raising deformation exclude the remaining ADM endpoints.
- **claim-supported-constraint-inverses** (construction, [source](#stmt-en-compact-inverses)): Fix a compact subannulus of $\{1<\|z\|<4\}$. A smooth scalar source $f$ supported there has a compactly supported symmetric solution $H$ of $\mathcal LH=f$ if its affine moments vanish. A smooth vector source $V$ has a compactly supported symmetric solution $k$ of $\mathcal Dk=V$ if its Killing moments vanish. The solutions can be supported in a fixed larger compact subannulus, and, for each integer $\ell\geq0$ and $1<p<\infty$, $$\label{en:inverse-estimates} \\|H\\|_{W^{\ell+2,p}}\leq C\\|f\\|_{W^{\ell,p}}, \qquad \\|k\\|_{W^{\ell+1,p}}\leq C\\|V\\|_{W^{\ell,p}}.$$
  - Explanation: Vanishing affine or Killing moments permit compactly supported inverses of the linearized scalar and momentum constraints, with the stated Sobolev gains.
- **claim-weak-end-replacement** (construction, [source](#stmt-en-annular-replacement)): Let $(g,K)$ have the weak end bounds of Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a>, integrable geometric constraint densities, and total DEC. Let $(g_*,K_*)$ be smooth vacuum reference data on that end with $g_*-\delta=O_\ell(r^{-1})$, $K_*=O_\ell(r^{-2})$ at every order, and the same ADM energy and momentum. For arbitrarily large $R$ there are smooth data $(\widehat g_R,\widehat K_R)$ equal to the original data on $r\leq R$ and to the reference on $r\geq4R$, such that on the intermediate annulus $$\label{en:annular-deficit} \widehat\mu_R-\|\widehat J_R\|_{\widehat g_R} \geq-\eta_RR^{-3},\qquad \eta_R\longrightarrow0.$$ For every fixed $1/2<\beta<\min(q,1)$ the scaled perturbations from Euclidean data are $O(R^{-\beta})$ in $C^2\times C^1$.
  - Explanation: An annular interpolation to vacuum reference data with the same ADM vector has a vanishing scaled energy-condition deficit while using only the original weak derivatives.
- **claim-rest-preparation** (construction, [source](#stmt-en-rest-preparation)): Let the data satisfy Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a> and $E>\|P\|$. Assume $\theta_+(S)\leq0$ on every boundary component. More generally, one may prescribe a fixed sign $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ on each component and assume $H+\sigma\operatorname{tr}_S K\leq0$ there. Set $m=\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|^2}$. There are smooth data $(g_j,K_j,\mathcal E_j,\mathcal B_j)$ on the same oriented exterior $\Omega$, with the same closed forms $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$, having the following properties.* 1. *Both charges are exactly $Q_E,Q_B$. Charged DEC is strict everywhere; for some $c_j>0$ and a fixed $0<\delta_0<1$, $$\inf_{\|Y\|_{g_j}\leq1}D_{g_j}(Y) \geq c_j r_y^{-3-\delta_0} \quad\hbox{on the far end}.$$ Every boundary component has strictly negative future expansion, or strictly negative prescribed expansion $H+\sigma\operatorname{tr}_S K$ in the fixed-sign variant.* 2. *In a rest chart $y$, $g_j-\delta=O_\ell(r_y^{-1})$ and $R_{g_j}=O_\ell(r_y^{-3-\delta_0})$ for every $\ell$. The tensor $K_j$ is compactly supported, and the two flux forms have components $O_1(r_y^{-2})$. The constraint densities are integrable and the metric is complete with $S$ included.* 3. *The rest ADM momentum is zero and its energy satisfies $E_j\to m$. The fields and tensors converge to the original data smoothly on every compact subset of $\Omega$.* 4. *There are $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ such that $g_j\geq(1-\epsilon_j)g$ on all of $\Omega$, and $$\label{en:area-convergence} A_{\min,g_j}(S)\longrightarrow A_{\min,g}(S).$$* *No uniform bound on the compact geometry of this sequence is asserted or needed. Each prepared datum is fixed before the subsequent elliptic comparison parameters are chosen.
  - Explanation: The original exterior is approximated by strict rest data with unchanged flux forms, convergent enclosing infima and energies tending to the original invariant mass.
- **claim-controlled-filling** (construction, [source](#stmt-sy-filled-setup)): For every sufficiently large integer $N$, the prepared exterior is contained in a smooth complete, boundaryless, one-ended manifold $\Omega_N$. Its metric and symmetric tensor extend $g,K$ and have the following properties. Each $S_i$ has a fixed inner collar on whose cross-sections $H+\sigma_i\operatorname{tr}_{\rm tan}K<0$, with the normal directed toward the exterior. Behind this collar there is a fixed transition to a product cylinder, a product neck of length $O(1+N)$, and a fixed cap. On the product neck and cap, $K=-\sigma_iL_0g$ for a fixed sufficiently large $L_0$. Local coordinate bounds for the metric, its inverse, and the tensor, of every fixed derivative order, and a positive local injectivity radius can be chosen independently of $N$. The enlarged compact core has volume $O(1+N)$. The extension of $r$ can be chosen uniformly comparable to one there. The closed flux forms $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ are retained on the original exterior.
  - Explanation: Artificial collars, necks and caps extend the prepared metric and tensor with uniform local geometry. Flux forms remain confined to their physical exterior role.
- **claim-exact-filled-scalar-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-sy-scalar-identity)): For every pair of smooth functions $f,Z$ on the filled manifold, $$\label{sy:scalar-equation} \frac12e^{2t}R_{\widehat g} =\mu+J(w)+\mathcal T+w(F)-F\tau -u^{-1}\operatorname{div}_g V.$$ The quadratic expression in Equation <a href="#sy:invariant-T" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sy:invariant-T">[sy:invariant-T]</a> has the following exact block expansion: $$\label{sy:expanded-T} \begin{aligned} \mathcal T={}&\tfrac12\|T^0\|^2+\|M+s_pa_wy\|^2 -\tfrac14v\|y\|^2+2s_p(\|y\|^2+dx^2)\\ &-\tfrac14(F-\chi j)^2+\chi j^2-\chi Fj+F^2 +2s_p\chi ja_wx. \end{aligned}$$ These identities require neither a constraint inequality nor a field extension to the filling.
  - Explanation: The transformed scalar curvature has an exact constraint, quadratic and divergence decomposition, independently of energy inequalities or electromagnetic extensions into the filling.
- **claim-polynomial-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-sy-coercivity)): For all the variables in Equation <a href="#sy:variables" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sy:variables">[sy:variables]</a>, $$\label{sy:coercivity-estimate} \|T\|^2+\|M\|^2+dj^2+F^2+\|dt\|_{A_d}^2 \le20(1+N)^2\mathcal T.$$ At a point where $dt=0$, set $\mathcal E_0=\|T^0\|^2+\|M\|^2+F^2+\chi j^2$. Then, independently of $N$, $$\label{sy:stationary-coercivity} \tfrac12\mathcal E_0\le\mathcal T\le\mathcal E_0.$$
  - Explanation: The quadratic scalar controls the weighted block variables with polynomial parameter loss, and at stationary points its comparison constants are independent of the filling parameter.
- **claim-stationary-point-subtraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-sy-stationary-minimum)): At any point where $dt=0$, $$\label{sy:stationary-identity} \begin{aligned} \tfrac12e^{2t}R_{\widehat g} ={}&\tfrac12R_g-v\operatorname{Ric}_g(e,e)+\mathcal S(H^f)\\ &-vp\operatorname{tr}_{e^\perp}\nabla^2t -2\operatorname{tr}_{A_d}\nabla^2t, \end{aligned}$$ and $$\label{sy:stationary-subtraction} \mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f) \ge\tfrac1{12}\mathcal T -(6N+25)\bigl(vF^2+\|K\|^2\bigr).$$ In particular both Hessian terms in Equation <a href="#sy:stationary-identity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sy:stationary-identity">[sy:stationary-identity]</a> are nonpositive at a local minimum of $t$.
  - Explanation: A stationary-point Gauss identity and algebraic subtraction isolate a positive coercive contribution with controlled tensor and trace errors.
- **claim-zero-tensor-reduction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-sy-zero-trace-reduction)): Every smooth zero-Dirichlet solution of the trace equation with $K=0$ has $f=0$. On that segment $t=Z$, $d=\chi=1$, $w=0$, and the second equation becomes $$\label{sy:scalar-end-system} 2\Delta_gZ+2(1+p(Z))\|dZ\|^2 =b\{2\delta_0s_p(Z)\|dZ\|^2+\rho-m_0(Z)C_N\rho_0\}.$$ In particular, at $(a,b)=(0,0)$ the unique solution is $f=Z=0$.
  - Explanation: The zero-tensor trace equation forces zero height and reduces the coupled problem to a scalar equation with a unique zero solution at the terminal homotopy point.
- **claim-uniform-height-outer-slope** (bound, [source](#stmt-es-height)): There are constants $C,r_0$, independent of $N$, such that every smooth solution of the trace equation in <a href="#es:homotopy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="es:homotopy">[es:homotopy]</a> satisfies $$\label{es:height-bound} \|h\|\le C, \qquad \|h\|\le C(r^{-b_1}-R^{-b_1})\quad(r_0\le r\le R),$$ provided $R\ge2r_0$. On the outer sphere, $$\label{es:face-slope} \|df\|_g\le C\eta^{-1}R^{-b_1-1}.$$ Consequently, for all $R\ge R_{\min}(N,\epsilon)$, one has $t>-\epsilon$ on that sphere. If $a=0$, then $f=h=0$.
  - Explanation: Maximum principles and radial barriers bound the rescaled height and the outer slope uniformly in the filling parameter, placing the outer face strictly above the floor.
- **claim-floor-exclusion** (bound, [source](#stmt-es-floor)): One can choose a fixed $\delta_0>0$ and a polynomial $C_N$ such that no smooth solution of <a href="#es:homotopy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="es:homotopy">[es:homotopy]</a> with $t\ge-\epsilon$ touches $t=-\epsilon$, provided $R\ge R_{\min}(N,\epsilon)$. The choices are uniform in the homotopy parameters.
  - Explanation: A polynomial penalty prevents a smooth above-floor solution from touching the floor anywhere along the homotopy.
- **claim-high-level-moment** (bound, [source](#stmt-es-high-integral)): On the first segment $b=1$ of <a href="#es:homotopy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="es:homotopy">[es:homotopy]</a>, there is a polynomial $Z_0=P_N\ge2$ such that $$\label{es:high-sign} \Xi\ge\delta_0\mathcal T+\rho+\tfrac12\delta_0G \qquad\hbox{where }Z>Z_0.$$ Every fixed enlargement of $\mathcal C_N$ satisfies $$\label{es:moment} \int_{\mathcal C_N} e^Z\,d\nu\le\exp(P_N).$$ The constants are independent of $R$ and $a$.
  - Explanation: Above a polynomial level the scalar source is positive, and divergence testing bounds an exponential moment over the enlarged core.
- **claim-graph-sobolev-estimate** (bound, [source](#stmt-es-sobolev)): For each of the core patches just described, and every smooth compactly supported function $\varphi$ in the patch, $$\label{es:sobolev-form} \left(\int\|\varphi\|^6\,d\nu\right)^{1/3} \le S_N\int\bigl(\|d\varphi\|_A^2 +(1+\mathcal T)\varphi^2\bigr)\,d\nu, \qquad \log S_N\le P_N.$$ No bound on $Z$, $df$, or derivatives of $t$ is required beyond $t\ge-\epsilon$ and the trace and coercivity identities.
  - Explanation: A submanifold Sobolev inequality controls graph-patch test functions using the weighted gradient and coercive density without assuming slope or distortion bounds in advance.
- **claim-normalized-energy-estimate** (bound, [source](#stmt-es-energy)): There are polynomials $E_N$ and $s_0(N)\ge1$ such that on the first homotopy segment, for $s\ge s_0(N)$ and any compactly supported base cutoff $\psi$, $$\label{es:energy-form} \int\psi^2e^{2sZ}\bigl(\mathcal T+s\|dZ\|_A^2\bigr)\,d\nu \le E_N(1+s)\int e^{2sZ} (\psi^2+\|d\psi\|_g^2)\,d\nu.$$ All constants are independent of $R$, $a$, and the solution.
  - Explanation: Testing with a normalized exponential weight controls coercive density and scalar gradient energy with polynomial coefficients.
- **claim-quantitative-distortion** (bound, [source](#stmt-es-distortion)): For the choices in Lemma <a href="#es:floor" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="es:floor">29</a>, every smooth solution of <a href="#es:homotopy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="es:homotopy">[es:homotopy]</a> with $t\ge-\epsilon$ and $R\ge R_{\min}(N,\epsilon)$ satisfies $$\label{es:distortion-bound} -\epsilon<t\le Z\le P_N,\qquad \ell\le l\le e,\qquad \|f\|+\|df\|_g\le\exp(P_N).$$ The polynomial is independent of the outer radius and the homotopy parameters. In particular, exhausting the exterior at fixed $N$ preserves these bounds.
  - Explanation: Moment bounds, graph Sobolev control and iteration give polynomial upper distortion bounds and exponential height-and-slope bounds independent of the outer truncation.
- **claim-rough-axial-gradient** (bound, [source](#stmt-so-rough-gradient)): Let $g$ range over metrics with uniform ellipticity and bounded local $C^2$ norms on a three-dimensional ball. Suppose that $z\in C^2$, $\|z\|+\|dz\|\le M$, and $$\label{so:axial-equation} A:\nabla^2z=G,\qquad A=I-(1-\chi)e\otimes e,\qquad e=\frac{\nabla z}{\|\nabla z\|},\qquad 0<c\le\chi\le1,\qquad \|G\|\le M,$$ where the axis at a zero of $dz$ may be arbitrary. No continuity assumption on $\chi$ is imposed. There are $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $C$ depending only on the displayed bounds and the patch geometry such that on every smaller patch $$\label{so:rough-estimates} [dz]_{C^\alpha}\le C,\qquad \int_{B_r(x)}\|\nabla^2z\|^2\,dV_g\le C r^{1+2\alpha}.$$ The same assertion holds up to a smooth face on which $z$ is constant; balls in the integral are then intersected with the domain. It is enough that $z$ be individually $C^1\cap W^{2,s}$ for every finite $s$ and $C^2$ up to each side of such a reflected face.
  - Explanation: An equation whose measurable axial coefficient follows the gradient direction still has uniform Hölder gradient and local Hessian-energy estimates without differentiating that coefficient.
- **claim-measure-potential-estimate** (bound, [source](#stmt-so-potential)): Let $M$ be a symmetric bounded measurable uniformly elliptic matrix on $B_r\subset\mathbb R^3$. If $\|B\|\le C_0$ and a nonnegative finite measure $\mu$ satisfies $\mu(B_s(x))\le C_0s^{1+\gamma}$ for some $0<\gamma<1$, then the zero-Dirichlet solution of $$-\operatorname{div}(MDv)=\operatorname{div}B+\mu$$ satisfies $\\|v\\|_\infty\le C(r+r^\gamma)$. The assertion applies uniformly to smooth approximations of the data and hence to their weak limits.
  - Explanation: Bounded divergence forcing and a measure with the specified growth give a small uniform potential bound for a measurable uniformly elliptic operator.
- **claim-coupled-smooth-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-so-coupled-regularity)): On a fixed truncation, every smooth solution of the homotopy in Equation <a href="#sy:homotopy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sy:homotopy">[sy:homotopy]</a> satisfying $t\ge-\epsilon$ has local smooth bounds depending only on the fixed data and $N$. The bounds hold on uniformly sized interior patches and on outer Dirichlet half-patches, independently of a sufficiently large truncation radius. In particular there is a fixed exponent $\alpha_0>0$ and a uniform local $C^{1,\alpha_0}$ bound for $f$ and $C^{0,\alpha_0}$ bound for $Z$.
  - Explanation: The rough axial estimate and a potential argument first control the height gradient and scalar oscillation, then permit smooth elliptic bootstrapping at fixed filling parameter.
- **claim-unrestricted-trial-trace** (theorem, [source](#stmt-so-trial-trace)): Fix a smooth compact truncation $\Omega_{N,R}$, $a\in[0,1]$, and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. For every $Z\in C^{1,\alpha}(\overline{\Omega_{N,R}})$, including trials for which the implicit $t$ is below $-\epsilon$, there is a unique solution $f\in C^{3,\alpha}(\overline{\Omega_{N,R}})$ of $$\operatorname{tr}_{A_\chi}(K_a+H^f)=\eta f, \qquad f\|_{\partial\Omega_{N,R}}=0.$$ The solution depends continuously on $(a,Z)$ in $C^{2,\alpha}$; bounded sets of trials have uniform bounds sufficient for this assertion. For $a=0$ the solution is identically zero.
  - Explanation: Every trial scalar in the stated Hölder class determines a unique trace solution, even below the eventual floor; this supplies a globally defined compact-map construction.
- **claim-filled-solver-normalized-end** (theorem, [source](#stmt-so-filled-solver)): For the choices in Section <a href="#sy:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sy:section">5</a>, Lemma <a href="#es:floor" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="es:floor">29</a>, and Proposition <a href="#es:distortion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="es:distortion">33</a>, every sufficiently large $N$ admits a smooth solution $(f,Z)$ of Equation <a href="#sy:system" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sy:system">[sy:system]</a> on the complete filled manifold $\Omega_N$. It satisfies $$-\epsilon<t\le Z\le\mathcal P_N,\qquad \ell\le l\le e,\qquad \|f\|+\|df\|\le\exp(\mathcal P_N).$$ The height estimates of Lemma <a href="#es:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="es:height">28</a> also hold. On the physical end, for each fixed integer $j\ge0$ there are $c_j,C_j>0$, allowed to depend on $N$, such that $$\label{so:physical-end} f=O_j(e^{-c_jr}),\qquad t,Z=O_j(r^{-1}),\qquad \Delta_g t=O(r^{-3-\beta}).$$ In particular both end constants are zero. The solution is obtained by exhausting the outer Dirichlet radius with $N$ fixed. For the resulting solution $u\Xi$ is absolutely integrable, $u\to1$, and the penalty vanishes sufficiently far out on the end.
  - Explanation: Degree theory and outer-radius exhaustion produce a smooth filled solution with strict floor separation, normalized physical end and integrable scalar source.
- **claim-filled-deformation-mass-cost** (bound, [source](#stmt-cp-mass-cost)): The metric $\widehat g$ has a well-defined ADM energy and $$\label{cp:mass-flux} E(\widehat g)=E_*-\frac{\mathfrak F_N}{8\pi}, \qquad \mathfrak F_N=\int_{\Omega_N}u\Xi\,dV_{g_N} =\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{r=R}g_N(V,\nu_R)\,dA_{g_N}.$$ There is a nonnegative sequence $a_N$ such that $$\label{cp:mass-error} E(\widehat g)\le E_*+a_N, \qquad a_N\le\mathcal P_N(\ell+\ell^{1/2})\longrightarrow0.$$
  - Explanation: The deformation energy is determined by a total divergence flux whose negative part tends to zero despite the artificial filling.
- **claim-collar-cap-height-gap** (bound, [source](#stmt-cp-height-gap)): The product lengths in Lemma <a href="#sy:filled-setup" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sy:filled-setup">23</a> can be chosen of order $O(1+N)$ so that a number $b_2>0$, independent of $N$, has the following property for all large $N$. On each cap, its product neck, and the associated original boundary component, $$\label{cp:signed-height} \sigma_i h<-b_2.$$ The inequality also holds on a neighborhood of that boundary component.
  - Explanation: Signed barriers on the collars, necks and caps separate every original boundary component from the low-height region by a fixed gap.
- **claim-low-band-curvature** (bound, [source](#stmt-cp-curvature)): For all large $N$, on the part of the original exterior where $\|h\|\le b_3$, $$\label{cp:curvature-lower} \frac{\lambda^2}{2}R_{\widetilde g}\ge I_g(w).$$ The modification $\psi$ is compactly supported. After the coordinate dilation $y'=e^\epsilon y$, the comparison metric is strongly asymptotically flat, has integrable scalar curvature, and its ADM mass $M_N$ satisfies $$\label{cp:comparison-mass} M_N=e^\epsilon E(\widehat g) \le e^\epsilon(E_*+a_N).$$
  - Explanation: The compact conformal plateau retains the charged curvature lower bound in the low-height region and changes the normalized ADM mass by the stated controlled amount.
- **claim-flux-preserving-projection** (construction, [source](#stmt-cp-flux-projection)): On the original exterior there are smooth closed two-forms $\widetilde\alpha_1,\widetilde\alpha_2$, with total fluxes $4\pi Q_E,4\pi Q_B$, whose associated vector fields in $\widetilde g$ satisfy $$\label{cp:charged-scalar} R_{\widetilde g}\ge 2\bigl(\|\widetilde{\mathcal E}\|_{\widetilde g}^2 +\|\widetilde{\mathcal B}\|_{\widetilde g}^2\bigr) \quad\hbox{where } \|h\|\le b_3.$$ The vector fields are divergence free and have $O_1(r^{-2})$ decay in the normalized end coordinates.
  - Explanation: A charge rotation and field projection preserve both total charges and give divergence-free comparison fields controlled by scalar curvature.
- **claim-outermost-minimal-enclosure** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cp-outermost-enclosure)): Let a smooth connected Riemannian three-manifold be complete with a nonempty compact smooth minimal boundary included. Suppose it has one end admitting a foliation by sufficiently large strictly mean-convex spheres, and that the maximum principle with these spheres confines every compact minimal enclosure to a bounded region. Then its inner boundary is enclosed by a compact smooth embedded outermost minimal full cut. The cut may be disconnected and may coincide with components of the given boundary. Its exterior is the connected component containing the end.
  - Explanation: A complete exterior with minimal inner boundary and confining mean-convex end spheres admits an outermost minimal full cut, allowing disconnectedness and boundary coincidence.
- **claim-minimizer-obstacle-avoidance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cp-contact-exclusion)): For all large $N$ there is a bounded finite-perimeter set $B_N$ containing $O_N$ whose full $\widetilde g$-perimeter is minimal among all such bounded sets. After filling bounded complementary pockets, its entire frontier $\Gamma_N^0$ is a nonempty compact smooth embedded minimal surface, disjoint from $O_N$, and its exterior is connected. Moreover $$\label{cp:competitor-bound} P_{\widetilde g}(B_N)\le e^{\mathcal P_N}.$$
  - Explanation: A perimeter minimizer encloses the thickened high-height obstacle but cannot touch it because plateau area cost exceeds the available competitor bound.
- **claim-charged-comparison-exterior** (construction, [source](#stmt-cp-charged-comparison)): For each fixed strict prepared exterior, each $\epsilon>0$, and all sufficiently large $N$, there is a smooth one-ended exterior $\widetilde\Omega_N\subset\operatorname{int}\Omega$, complete with its compact smooth boundary $\Gamma_N$ included, with the following properties. Its metric and fields are the restrictions of the comparison objects above; the boundary is outermost minimal, and $$\begin{aligned} \widetilde g&\ge g, &\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_{\widetilde g}(\Gamma_N)&\ge a_g(S), \label{cp:comparison-area}\\ \operatorname{div}_{\widetilde g}\widetilde{\mathcal E} &=\operatorname{div}_{\widetilde g}\widetilde{\mathcal B}=0, &R_{\widetilde g}&\ge 2\bigl(\|\widetilde{\mathcal E}\|_{\widetilde g}^2 +\|\widetilde{\mathcal B}\|_{\widetilde g}^2\bigr). \label{cp:comparison-dec} \end{aligned}$$ Its total charges are $Q_E,Q_B$. Its metric is $O_2(r^{-1})$ asymptotically flat, its fields are $O_1(r^{-2})$, and its scalar curvature is integrable. Its ADM mass satisfies $M_N\le e^\epsilon(E_*+a_N)$ with the error in Equation <a href="#cp:mass-error" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="cp:mass-error">[cp:mass-error]</a>.
  - Explanation: Removing the high-height region yields a charged Riemannian comparison exterior with outermost minimal boundary, area dominance, preserved total charges and controlled mass.
- **claim-prepared-charged-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-cp-numerical-prepared)): The strict prepared rest data satisfy $$\label{cp:prepared-inequality} E_*\ge Q, \qquad \sqrt{\frac{a_g(S)}{4\pi}} \le E_*+\sqrt{E_*^2-Q^2}.$$ This conclusion allows a different fixed choice of future or past boundary sign on each component.
  - Explanation: A bounded flux-profile solve converts charge into an exact energy decrease; the neutral enclosing-area theorem and profile optimization yield the charged prepared-data bound.
- **claim-equality-area-envelope** (theorem, [source](#stmt-va-area-envelope)): For a smooth path with initial metric derivative $h$, the right derivative of its enclosing-area infimum is $$\label{va:area-derivative} a'_+(0)=\min_{M\in\mathcal M_B}a'_M(h).$$
  - Explanation: On the equality exterior the right derivative of the enclosure infimum is the minimum area variation over all minimizing filled sets.
- **claim-positive-constraint-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-va-separation)): There are a probability measure $\pi_B$ on $\mathcal M_B$, a nonnegative locally finite measure $\Lambda_B$ on $\mathcal A_B$, and a nonnegative finite measure $\zeta_B$ on $B$, such that for every compact direction and every ADM prototype, $$\label{va:multiplier} 16\pi\mathcal L'-c\int_{\mathcal M_B}a'_M(h)\,d\pi_B(M) =\int_{\mathcal A_B}\mathfrak C'\,d\Lambda_B -\int_B\theta_\varepsilon'\,d\zeta_B.$$ The measure satisfies $\int\rho_*\,d\Lambda_B<\infty$.
  - Explanation: Separation of feasible variations from a positive cone yields nonnegative constraint and boundary measures and a probability measure on minimizing enclosures.
- **claim-normal-test-variations** (construction, [source](#stmt-va-gaussian-jets)): For each smooth compactly supported function $s$ in the open exterior of $B$, there are compact variations, indexed by $\delta>0$, for which $h'=2sK$, both flux-form variations are closed, and $\mathfrak C'\to0$ uniformly on the compact active-ray support. Consequently, $$\label{va:averaged-trace} \int_{\mathcal M_B}\int_{\partial M} s\operatorname{tr}_{T_M}K\,dA_g\,d\pi_B(M)=0.$$
  - Explanation: Gaussian finite jets produce closed-form variations whose active constraint derivative vanishes in the limit, forcing an averaged tangential-curvature trace identity.
- **claim-minimizing-sheet-trace** (theorem, [source](#stmt-va-trace-support)): For $\pi_B$-almost every minimizing set, $\operatorname{tr}_{T_M}K=0$ on its sheets in the open exterior of $B$.
  - Explanation: Compatibility of tangent planes prevents cancellation in the averaged trace identity and forces vanishing trace on almost every selected minimizing frontier.
- **claim-no-enlarged-marginal-obstacle** (theorem, [source](#stmt-va-enlarged-obstacle)): There is no full smooth enlarged obstacle $B$ of the type described at the start of this section which contains an additional open subset of $\Omega$ outside the original filled obstacle and is marginal with an arbitrary fixed choice of sign on each component. For the original obstacle, the area term in Equation <a href="#va:multiplier" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="va:multiplier">[va:multiplier]</a> is exactly $a'_S(h)=\tfrac12\int_S\operatorname{tr}_S h\,dA$.
  - Explanation: Original outermostness excludes any larger full marginal obstacle with fixed componentwise signs and localizes the area multiplier to the original boundary.
- **claim-smooth-multiplier-moments** (theorem, [source](#stmt-va-smooth-moments)): The moments have smooth densities on $\overline\Omega$, with no additional moment mass on $S$. In the interior they satisfy $$\label{va:shift-equation} \operatorname{sym}\nabla X=-uK.$$ Their full first jets obey a closed linear first-order system with smooth coefficients.
  - Explanation: Distributional adjoint equations regularize the multiplier moments, eliminate boundary atoms and close their first jets into a smooth linear system.
- **claim-multiplier-end-normalization** (bound, [source](#stmt-va-normalization)): For any $q_0$ with $1/2<q_0<\min(q,1)$, $$\label{va:asymptotic-moments} u=b^0+O_2(r^{-q_0}),\qquad X^i=b^i+O_2(r^{-q_0}).$$ Moreover $u>0$ in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$.
  - Explanation: Causality eliminates growing modes in the moment system, and ADM prototype tests fix the asymptotic lapse and shift. The lapse is positive in the open exterior.
- **claim-original-stationary-reconstruction** (construction, [source](#stmt-va-stationary-data)): On $\mathbb R\times\operatorname{int}\Omega$ there are smooth stationary fields $$\label{va:stationary-metric} \mathbf G=-u^2dz^2+g_{ij}(dx^i+X^i dz)(dx^j+X^j dz), \qquad \xi=\partial_z,$$ and a two-form $\mathbf F$, with the prescribed orientation, which induce all four original data $(g,K,\mathcal E,\mathcal B)$ on each constant-$z$ slice. The Killing field is nonzero and future causal, and tends to the unit future timelike vector $(E/m,-P/m)$ relative to the original asymptotic normal and frame. Both Maxwell equations hold. With $\mathsf S$ as in Equation <a href="#va:maxwell-stress" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="va:maxwell-stress">[va:maxwell-stress]</a>, $$\begin{aligned} u(\mathbf{Ein}_{ij}-\mathsf S_{ij}) &=-(J_m)_{(i}X_{j)},\label{va:spatial-stress}\\ \mathbf{Ein}-\mathsf S &=\frac{\mu_m}{u^2}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat. \label{va:null-stress} \end{aligned}$$ The coefficient is nonnegative; wherever it is positive, $\xi$ is null. In particular the region $W=-\mathbf G(\xi,\xi)=u^2-\|X\|_g^2>0$ is electrovacuum.
  - Explanation: The smooth lapse and shift reconstruct a stationary spacetime inducing the original tensors. Possible residual matter is a nonnegative stress aligned with a null Killing field.
- **claim-global-killing-potentials** (theorem, [source](#stmt-va-potentials)): The spatial one-forms $$\label{va:potential-forms} \beta_E=u\mathcal E^\flat+(\mathcal B\times X)^\flat, \qquad \beta_B=u\mathcal B^\flat+(X\times\mathcal E)^\flat$$ are globally exact on $\operatorname{int}\Omega$. They are the pullbacks of $i_\xi\mathbf F$ and $i_\xi(*_{\mathbf G}\mathbf F)$, respectively. Their potentials extend smoothly to $S$.
  - Explanation: Testing all compact closed flux-form variations eliminates every period of the Killing contractions, giving global scalar potentials without a simple-connectivity assumption.
- **claim-boundary-surface-gravity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-va-boundary)): The smooth multipliers on the original boundary satisfy $$\label{va:boundary-identities} X=u\nu,\qquad \partial_\nu u+K(X,\nu)=\kappa, \qquad \kappa=\frac c2>0.$$ Either $u>0$ everywhere on connected $S$, or $u=0$ everywhere there. In the first case, $$\label{va:horizon-gradient} dW=2\kappa X^\flat\quad\text{on }S.$$ In the second case, in original outward normal distance $s$, $$\label{va:bifurcation-expansion} u=\kappa s+O(s^2),\qquad X=O(s^2).$$ In both cases $W>0$ on a deleted collar of $S$. The coefficient $h_*=\mu_m/u^2$ in Equation <a href="#va:null-stress" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="va:null-stress">[va:null-stress]</a> is a smooth nonnegative function supported in a compact subset of $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, and extends by zero through $S$.
  - Explanation: Boundary variations fix the normal shift and positive surface gravity. Connectedness gives a positive-or-zero lapse dichotomy, and both cases have an electrovacuum deleted collar.
- **claim-bilateral-end-communication** (theorem, [source](#stmt-st-communication)): Let $\mathfrak E=\mathbb R\times\{\rho>R\}$, with $R$ sufficiently large. Taking chronological past and future within $\mathfrak R$, one has $$I^-(\mathfrak E)=\mathfrak R=I^+(\mathfrak E).$$
  - Explanation: A noncommunicating boundary would create an excluded larger marginal obstacle, so every stationary interior point communicates chronologically with the distant end in both directions.
- **claim-smooth-invariant-boundary-jets** (theorem, [source](#stmt-st-covariant-jets)): Suppose $u\|_S=0$. The tensors $\boldsymbol\nabla^j\mathbf F$ and $\boldsymbol\nabla^j\mathbf{Rm}$, for every integer $j\geq0$, have smooth one-sided limiting coefficients at $S$ in this frame. So does $\boldsymbol\nabla\xi$. At $S$ the latter tensor is the endomorphism $B$ given by $$\label{st:boost-generator} B\nu=\kappa n,\qquad Bn=\kappa\nu, \qquad B\|_{TS}=0.$$ Every limiting curvature and Maxwell jet is invariant under $B$, acting on all its tensor and derivative slots. It is also invariant under the map $I_b$ which reverses both $n$ and $\nu$ and fixes $TS$.
  - Explanation: When the lapse vanishes at the boundary, all curvature and Maxwell covariant jets have smooth one-sided limits invariant under the normal boost and simultaneous normal reversal.
- **claim-smooth-normal-parity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-st-smooth-parity)): Let $a(r,y)$ be smooth for $r\geq0$, with $y$ in a compact smooth manifold. If all odd $r$-derivatives vanish at $r=0$, then $a(r,y)=a_0(r^2,y)$ for a function $a_0$ smooth up to $r^2=0$. If all even derivatives vanish, then $a(r,y)=r a_1(r^2,y)$ with $a_1$ smooth. Both assertions hold for tensor coefficients in smooth local frames and uniformly with all tangential derivatives.
  - Explanation: Vanishing odd or even normal jets allows smooth dependence on squared distance, with an additional radial factor in the odd case, including smooth flat remainders.
- **claim-smooth-bifurcation-attachment** (construction, [source](#stmt-st-attachment)): There is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian manifold $(\widetilde{\mathfrak R},\mathbf G)$ containing $\mathfrak R$ and a compact smooth spacelike surface $B_0$ naturally identified with $S$, such that the following properties hold.* 1. *The Killing field extends smoothly, has complete flow, vanishes on $B_0$, and is a nondegenerate boost in its normal plane with constant $\kappa$.* 2. *The two-form $\mathbf F$ has a smooth invariant extension. The field equations continue to hold on the original right wedge.* 3. *A neighborhood of the added surfaces is a band $\{\|UV\|<p_0\}\times S$, with $$\xi=\kappa(V\partial_V-U\partial_U),\qquad B_0=\{U=V=0\},$$ and its overlap with $\mathfrak R$ is $U,V>0$.* 4. *If $u\|_S>0$, the original stationary chart extends to the future horizon $U=0,V>0$, with each original boundary section at a finite positive $V$. If $u\|_S=0$, the original slice extends to $B_0$. In both cases the metric of $B_0$ is the original metric on $S$.
  - Explanation: Smooth invariant coefficient extensions attach a bifurcation band with complete Killing flow and smooth Maxwell field while retaining field equations on the original right wedge.
- **claim-strong-stationary-end** (bound, [source](#stmt-st-stationary-end)): The stationary end admits coordinates $(t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with $\xi=\partial_t$. Writing $\rho=\|x\|$ in this chart, one has for every fixed integer $j\geq0$ $$\label{st:strong-end} \mathbf G_{ab}-\eta_{ab}=O_j(\rho^{-1}),\qquad \mathbf F_{ab}=O_j(\rho^{-2}).$$ All these estimates have the corresponding scaled Hölder bounds. The coordinates are obtained from a constant rest chart by stationary corrections $O_{2,\gamma}(\rho^{1-q_1})$, where $1/2<q_1<q_0<\min(q,1)$ and $0<\gamma<1$ can be chosen smaller as needed. In particular, on the end the orbit metric $h_s$ satisfies $h_s-\delta=O_j(\rho^{-1})$ and $W=1+O_j(\rho^{-1})$.
  - Explanation: Stationary harmonic coordinates and elliptic bootstrapping upgrade weak original decay to strong metric and Maxwell end bounds of every fixed derivative order.
- **claim-global-temporal-cauchy-graph** (construction, [source](#stmt-st-temporal-graph)): There is a smooth function $s_0$ on $\mathfrak R$ satisfying $\xi(s_0)=1$, whose differential is timelike, such that $$\label{st:time-near-bifurcation} s_0=\frac{1}{2\kappa}\log\frac VU$$ near the attachment and $s_0=t+\mathrm{constant}$ on the harmonic rest end of Proposition <a href="#st:stationary-end" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="st:stationary-end">62</a>. Each level of $s_0$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $\mathfrak R$.
  - Explanation: A global temporal function joins the bifurcation time to rest time, and causal speed bounds make each level Cauchy in the right wedge.
- **claim-attachment-causality-domain** (theorem, [source](#stmt-st-attachment-causality)): After decreasing the width of the added band, the full spacetime $\widetilde{\mathfrak R}$ is strongly causal and $\Sigma$ is acausal. Moreover $$\label{st:domain-equality} \operatorname{int}D_{\widetilde{\mathfrak R}}(\Sigma)=\mathfrak R.$$ The equality holds using either inextendible causal curves or the timelike-curve convention for domains of dependence.
  - Explanation: A sufficiently narrow attachment is strongly causal, the completed reference slice is acausal, and its open domain of dependence is precisely the original right wedge.
- **claim-maximal-cauchy-hypersurface** (theorem, [source](#stmt-st-maximal-slice)): Fix $q_2\in(1/2,1)$. There exists a smooth spacelike maximal hypersurface $\widehat\Sigma\subset\widetilde{\mathfrak R}$ with $\partial\widehat\Sigma=B_0$, whose interior is Cauchy in $\mathfrak R$. Every complete Killing orbit of $\mathfrak R$ meets it exactly once. In the harmonic rest chart of Proposition <a href="#st:stationary-end" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="st:stationary-end">62</a> its end is a graph $t=f(x)$ satisfying $$\label{st:maximal-decay} f=O(\rho^{1-q_2}),\qquad \partial f=O(\rho^{-q_2}),\qquad \partial^2 f=O(\rho^{-1-q_2}).$$ The graph has the corresponding higher differentiability and scaled Hölder estimates. Its Killing translates cover the right wedge.
  - Explanation: The verified attachment and communication conditions permit a smooth maximal Cauchy hypersurface with the actual bifurcation boundary and controlled rest-end graph.
- **claim-maximal-boundary-orbit-graph** (theorem, [source](#stmt-st-maximal-boundary-graph)): The Killing graph over $\widehat\Sigma$ respects the whole original orbit space. On its boundary collar the projection is a smooth diffeomorphism when the orbit space is given the defining function $r=\sqrt{UV}$. The global electric and magnetic Killing potentials from Lemma <a href="#va:potentials" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="va:potentials">55</a> pull back to exact smooth potentials on $\widehat\Sigma$, smooth up to $B_0$ and constant there.
  - Explanation: The maximal slice projects smoothly to the entire orbit space in its appropriate boundary defining function, and both scalar Killing potentials extend constantly to the bifurcation boundary.
- **claim-maximal-original-orbit-identification** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ri-orbit-graph)): Let $\Sigma'$ be the maximal hypersurface of Proposition <a href="#st:maximal-slice" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="st:maximal-slice">65</a>, and let $B_0$ be its bifurcation boundary. Projection along the Killing flow identifies $\operatorname{int}\Sigma'$ diffeomorphically with $\operatorname{int}\Omega$. This identification takes the end to the same end and identifies the boundary labels on $B_0$ with those on $S$. Compact cuts contained in the interiors of the two hypersurfaces, with corresponding orbit labels, are homologous in the right wedge.
  - Explanation: Each causal Killing orbit meets the maximal slice once, identifying the open orbit spaces, boundary labels and end, with corresponding compact cuts homologous in the right wedge.
- **claim-staticity-matter-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ri-staticity)): On $\Sigma'$ one has $$K'=0,\qquad X'=0,\qquad \mathcal B'=0.$$ The Killing field is strictly timelike throughout the open right wedge, and its metric and rotated Maxwell form have the global form $$\label{ri:static-product} \mathbf G=-(u')^2dT^2+g',\qquad \widehat{\mathbf F}=u'\,dT\wedge(\mathcal E')^\flat, \qquad u'=\sqrt W.$$ The residual non-electromagnetic stress vanishes. The original constraint densities $\mu_m,J_m$ consequently vanish on all of $\Omega$, including $S$.
  - Explanation: The magnetic-potential and momentum integrals force zero maximal-slice second form, shift and rotated magnetic field. The Killing field becomes timelike and all original additional matter vanishes.
- **claim-static-energy-original-mass** (theorem, [source](#stmt-ri-static-mass)): The metric $g'$ is complete up to $B_0$, has one strongly asymptotically flat end, and in its stationary rest coordinates $$g'_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_2(r^{-1}),\qquad \mathcal E'=O_1(r^{-2}),\qquad E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(g')=m.$$ Its electric charge is $Q$ and its magnetic charge is zero.
  - Explanation: The complete static orbit metric has the original invariant ADM mass and the rotated charges, with strong asymptotic decay.
- **claim-static-reissner-nordstrom-identification** (classification, [source](#stmt-ri-rn-identification)): There is an orientation-preserving isometry from $(\Sigma',g')$ onto the canonical exterior Reissner–Nordström slice of mass $m$ and charge magnitude $Q$, including its boundary. Under this isometry, with $r$ the areal radius, $$\label{ri:rn-static-data} g'=f^{-1}dr^2+r^2\sigma_2,\qquad \mathcal E'=\frac Q{r^2}\sqrt f\,\partial_r,\qquad u'=\sqrt f,\qquad f=1-\frac{2m}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2},\quad r\geq r_h.$$
  - Explanation: Connected-horizon electrostatic uniqueness identifies the closed static exterior, normalized lapse and electric field with the canonical Reissner–Nordström system.
- **claim-global-original-horizon-embedding** (construction, [source](#stmt-ri-original-embedding)): The original stationary section $z=0$ gives a smooth orientation-preserving spacelike embedding of all of $\Omega$ into one Reissner–Nordström exterior together with its future horizon or bifurcation sphere. It induces the original $(g,K,\mathcal E,\mathcal B)$, including their values on $S$, and its end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity.
  - Explanation: The original stationary section embeds globally and smoothly through the appropriate future horizon or bifurcation sphere, recovering its original second form and both signed electromagnetic fields.
- **claim-static-nonstatic-boosted-equality-examples** (construction, [source](#stmt-ri-sharp-examples)): For every $M>\sqrt{q_E^2+q_B^2}$ there are admissible equality data of each of the following kinds: static data; data with $K\not\equiv0$; and data with nonzero ADM momentum. In the last family, for every sufficiently small nonzero vector $v$, the actual ADM energy and momentum are $$E=\gamma M,\qquad P=\gamma Mv,\qquad \gamma=(1-\|v\|^2)^{-1/2},$$ with the positive-$K$ convention of this paper. In all three families the actual outward charges are $q_E,q_B$ and the original minimum enclosing area is $4\pi R_+^2$.
  - Explanation: Explicit static, compact radial-graph and cutoff boosted slices satisfy the full hypotheses and attain equality, with actual ADM fluxes and the full-cut area verified directly.

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-en-adm-flux",
        "exact_quote": "Let $G=\\eta+h$ be a Lorentzian metric on an exterior region containing the spacelike planes under consideration and the portions of their connecting cylinders at large radius. In background inertial coordinates suppose, uniformly on these regions, $$h=O_2(r^{-q_0}),\\qquad q_0>1/2,\\qquad\n \\operatorname{Ein}(G)=O(r^{-4}).$$ Use signature $(-+++)$ and the positive second-form convention $K(U,V)=G(\\nabla_U n,V)$. If the ADM limits on one plane exist, they exist on every fixed uniformly spacelike plane, and they are the components of the same translation covector $\\mathcal C$: $$\\label{en:translation-covector}\n \\mathcal C(a)=E a^0+\\sum_iP_i a^i.$$ In particular, if $E>|P|$ and $m=(E^2-|P|^2)^{1/2}$, the unit future vector $b=(E/m,-P/m)$ satisfies $\\mathcal C(b)=m$.*\n\n*The same conclusion applies to a stationary vacuum or electrovacuum end whenever these estimates hold in its stationary coordinates, after a constant linear change making its limiting metric Minkowski. In coordinates adapted to a stationary field with unit timelike limit, suppose the shift has order $O_1(r^{-q_0})$. Then the energy of a rest plane equals that of the spatial orbit metric.         "exact_quote": "Fix a compact subannulus of $\\{1<|z|<4\\}$. Charged DEC is strict everywhere; for some $c_j>0$ and a fixed $0<\\delta_0<1$, $$\\inf_{|Y|_{g_j}\\leq1}D_{g_j}(Y)\n           \\geq c_j r_y^{-3-\\delta_0}\n           \\quad\\hbox{on the far end}.$$ Every boundary component has strictly negative future expansion, or strictly negative prescribed expansion $H+\\sigma\\operatorname{tr}_S K$ in the fixed-sign variant.*\n\n2.  *In a rest chart $y$, $g_j-\\delta=O_\\ell(r_y^{-1})$ and $R_{g_j}=O_\\ell(r_y^{-3-\\delta_0})$ for every $\\ell$. The tensor $K_j$ is compactly supported, and the two flux forms have components $O_1(r_y^{-2})$. The constraint densities are integrable and the metric is complete with $S$ included.*\n\n3.  *The rest ADM momentum is zero and its energy satisfies $E_j\\to m$. The fields and tensors converge to the original data smoothly on every compact subset of $\\Omega$.*\n\n\n4.  *There are $\\epsilon_j\\downarrow0$ such that $g_j\\geq(1-\\epsilon_j)g$ on all of $\\Omega$, and $$\\label{en:area-convergence}\n      A_{\\min,g_j}(S)\\longrightarrow A_{\\min,g}(S).$$*\n\n*No uniform bound on the compact geometry of this sequence is asserted or needed. Each prepared datum is fixed before the subsequent elliptic comparison parameters are chosen.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-sy-filled-setup",
        "exact_quote": "For every sufficiently large integer $N$, the prepared exterior is contained in a smooth complete, boundaryless, one-ended manifold $\\Omega_N$. Its metric and symmetric tensor extend $g,K$ and have the following properties. Each $S_i$ has a fixed inner collar on whose cross-sections $H+\\sigma_i\\operatorname{tr}_{\\rm tan}K<0$, with the normal directed toward the exterior. Behind this collar there is a fixed transition to a product cylinder, a product neck of length $O(1+N)$, and a fixed cap. On the product neck and cap, $K=-\\sigma_iL_0g$ for a fixed sufficiently large $L_0$. Local coordinate bounds for the metric, its inverse, and the tensor, of every fixed derivative order, and a positive local injectivity radius can be chosen independently of $N$. The enlarged compact core has volume $O(1+N)$. The extension of $r$ can be chosen uniformly comparable to one there. The closed flux forms $\\alpha_1,\\alpha_2$ are retained on the original exterior.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.1"
      },

        "exact_quote": "On a fixed truncation, every smooth solution of the homotopy in Equation <a href=\"#sy:homotopy\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sy:homotopy\">[sy:homotopy]</a> satisfying $t\\ge-\\epsilon$ has local smooth bounds depending only on the fixed data and $N$.           "anchor": "stmt-va-boundary",

In the first case, $$\\label{va:horizon-gradient}\n dW=2\\kappa X^\\flat\\quad\\text{on }S.$$ In the second case, in original outward normal distance $s$, $$\\label{va:bifurcation-expansion}\n u=\\kappa s+O(s^2),\\qquad X=O(s^2).$$ In both cases $W>0$ on a deleted collar of $S$.           "anchor": "stmt-st-smooth-parity",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Charged exterior data** ([source](#stmt-def-data)): Let $\Omega$ be a connected oriented smooth three-manifold with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$, and let $(g,K,\mathcal E,\mathcal B)$ be smooth up to $S$. Here $g$ is Riemannian, $K$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ are vector fields. We require completeness of the metric space $(\Omega,g)$ with its boundary included. Outside a compact set there is exactly one coordinate end, diffeomorphic to $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\|x\|>R_0\}$. Throughout the proof we use geometric constraint densities: $$\begin{aligned} 2\mu&=R_g+\tau^2-\|K\|_g^2, & J_i&=\nabla^j(K_{ij}-\tau g_{ij}), &\tau&=\operatorname{tr}_gK, \label{eq:constraints}\\ \mu_m&=\mu-(\|\mathcal E\|_g^2+\|\mathcal B\|_g^2), & J_m&=J-2(\mathcal E\times\mathcal B)^\flat.&& \label{eq:matter} \end{aligned}$$ These four densities are $8\pi$ times their physical counterparts. The cross product uses the orientation of $\Omega$. Assume $$\label{eq:charged-dec} \mu_m\ge \|J_m\|_g,\qquad \operatorname{div}_g\mathcal E=\operatorname{div}_g\mathcal B=0, \qquad \mu,\|J\|_g\in L^1(\Omega,dV_g).$$ On the end, for some $q>1/2$ and $r=\|x\|$, assume $$\label{eq:weak-decay} g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K_{ij}=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\qquad \mathcal E^i,\mathcal B^i=O_1(r^{-2}).$$ The notation $O_j(r^{-a})$ bounds every coordinate derivative of order $\ell\le j$ by $C_\ell r^{-a-\ell}$. These are bounds on otherwise smooth data, not additional higher-derivative decay assumptions. The following limits are assumed finite: $$\begin{aligned} E&=\frac1{16\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{r=R}(\partial_jg_{ij}-\partial_ig_{jj})n_\delta^i\,dA_\delta, \label{eq:adm-energy}\\ P_i&=\frac1{8\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{r=R}(K_{ij}-\tau g_{ij})n_\delta^j\,dA_\delta, \label{eq:adm-momentum}\\ Q_E&=\frac1{4\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{r=R}g(\mathcal E,\nu_R)\,dA_g, &Q_B&=\frac1{4\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{r=R}g(\mathcal B,\nu_R)\,dA_g. \label{eq:charges} \end{aligned}$$ Here $n_\delta,dA_\delta$ are Euclidean, whereas $\nu_R,dA_g$ are computed in $g$. Put $Q=(Q_E^2+Q_B^2)^{1/2}$.
- **Full enclosing cut and enclosing-area radius** ([source](#stmt-def-full-cut)): A full enclosing cut is $\Gamma=\partial D$, the entire intrinsic manifold boundary of a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\subset\Omega$ that is closed in $\Omega$, has manifold interior in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, and contains the whole sufficiently distant part of the end. The boundary $\Gamma$ is required to be compact, smooth, embedded and two-sided. It is oriented toward the end. All components, including any portions coincident with $S$, are counted. In particular $D=\Omega$ contributes $\Gamma=S$. Define, in the original metric, $$\label{eq:enclosing-area} a_g(S)=\inf_\Gamma\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(\Gamma),\qquad r_A=\sqrt{\frac{a_g(S)}{4\pi}}.$$
- **Connected horizon class** ([source](#stmt-def-rigidity-class)): Data in Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical">3</a> belong to the connected horizon class if $S$ is connected, $\theta_+=0$ on $S$, every full cut has area at least $A=\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(S)>0$, and there is no compact smooth embedded two-sided full enclosing surface entirely in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$ with $\theta_+\le0$ everywhere. Such an excluded surface may be disconnected. Thus $a_g(S)=A$. No strictly positive stability eigenvalue of this marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS) is assumed.
- **Closed electromagnetic flux forms** ([source](#eq:flux-forms)): No assumption is made about data behind $S$, and no extension across $S$ is required. In particular, the single-end assumption concerns this exterior only. Boundary components and compact-interior topology are unrestricted. There is no assumption of a global electromagnetic vector potential. It is useful to retain instead the closed two-forms $$\label{eq:flux-forms} \alpha_1=\iota_{\mathcal E}dV_g,\qquad \alpha_2=\iota_{\mathcal B}dV_g.$$ Unless stated otherwise, a change of metric keeps these forms fixed and defines the new vector fields by contraction with the new volume form. All form norms are exterior-algebra norms.
- **Auxiliary obstacle perimeter minimum** ([source](#ct:perimeter-infimum)): For a bounded set $M$ of finite perimeter, let $P_g(M)=\|D\mathbf1_M\|_g(\widehat\Omega)$. Sets are initially identified up to volume-null sets. Put $$\label{ct:perimeter-infimum} p_g(F)=\inf\{P_g(M):M\text{ bounded, of finite perimeter, } F\subset M\text{ a.e.}\}.$$ Perimeter is taken in all of $\widehat\Omega$; in particular $P_g(F)=\operatorname{Area}_g(S)$. The same construction applies to any smooth compact enlarged obstacle whose exterior is connected and has the same end.
- **Minimizing filled-set family** ([source](#ct:variation-subsection)): For a fixed smooth obstacle $F$, denote the family of its minimizing filled sets by $\mathcal M_g(F)$.
- **Charged ball-test deficit** ([source](#en:ball-tests)): $$\label{en:ball-tests} \begin{split} I_g(Y)&=\|X_1\|_g^2+\|X_2\|_g^2 +2\langle X_1\times X_2,Y\rangle_g,\\ D_g(Y)&=\mu+J(Y)-I_g(Y) =\mu_{\mathrm m}+J_{\mathrm m}(Y). \end{split}$$ The inequality $2\|X_1\times X_2\|\leq \|X_1\|^2+\|X_2\|^2$ gives $I_g(Y)\geq0$, and $$\inf_{\|Y\|_g\leq1}D_g(Y)=\mu_{\mathrm m}-\|J_{\mathrm m}\|_g.$$ Consequently charged DEC implies total DEC. A constant $SO(2)$ rotation of $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ preserves both $I_g$ and $D_g$: it preserves the sum of the squared norms and the cross product.
- **Compression functions** ([source](#sy:compression-functions)): $$\label{sy:compression-functions} p(t)=N\vartheta(Nt),\qquad l(t)=\exp\left(\int_0^t p(s)\,ds\right),\qquad \ell=e^{-N\epsilon},\qquad \eta=\ell^{3/2}.$$ We have $l'=pl$, $0\le p\le N$, $l(t)=e^{Nt}$ for $t\le0$, and $1\le l(t)\le e$ for $t\ge0$. In particular, $$\label{sy:l-bounds} \ell\le l(t)\le e\quad\hbox{if }t\ge-\epsilon.$$
- **Implicit scalar variable** ([source](#sy:implicit-t)): For unknown smooth functions $f,Z$, define $t$ by $$\label{sy:implicit-t} Z=t+\frac14\log D,\qquad D=1+l(t)^2\|df\|_g^2.$$ This definition is global, including for trial functions that do not satisfy a lower bound on $t$. Indeed, for fixed $\xi\in T_x^*\Omega_N$, the derivative of the right side with respect to $t$ is $1+pv/2\ge1$, where $v=l(t)^2\|\xi\|^2/(1+l(t)^2\|\xi\|^2)$. Its limits are $-\infty$ and $+\infty$ at the two ends of the real line: at the negative end $l=e^{Nt}$, and at the positive end $l$ is constant. The implicit function theorem therefore gives a unique smooth $t=t(x,Z,\xi)$, with no singularity at $\xi=0$.
- **Filled geometric variables** ([source](#sy:variables)): Vectors and covectors are identified using $g$. Our notation is $$\label{sy:variables} \begin{aligned} w&=lD^{-1/2}\nabla f,& a_w&=\|w\|,& v&=a_w^2,& d&=D^{-1}=1-v,\\ q&=2+pv,& \chi&=\frac{2d}{q},& A_d&=I-w\otimes w,& A_\chi&=I-\frac{2+p}{q}w\otimes w,\\ U&=l\sqrt D,& u&=e^tU,& h&=\eta f,& H^f&=lD^{-1/2}\nabla^2 f,\\ C&=K+H^f,& F&=\operatorname{tr}_{A_\chi}C,& V&=u A_\chi(2\nabla Z+K(w,\cdot)),& \widehat g&=e^{2t}(g+l^2df^2). \end{aligned}$$ Here $\operatorname{tr}_A C=A^{ij}C_{ij}$. Both $A_d$ and $A_\chi$ have eigenvalue one perpendicular to $w$, and their axial eigenvalues are $d$ and $\chi$, respectively. Thus $0<\chi\le d\le1$, and $$\label{sy:axis-comparison} \frac{2}{2+N}A_d\le A_\chi\le A_d.$$ The symbols $q,d,\chi$ in this section are auxiliary scalar coefficients; $Q$ continues to denote the total charge.
- **Invariant quadratic scalar** ([source](#sy:invariant-T)): For symmetric tensors $A,B$, put $$\mathsf P_A=A-(\operatorname{tr}A)g,\qquad \mathsf B(A,B)=\langle A,B\rangle -(\operatorname{tr}A)(\operatorname{tr}B).$$ Let $$\label{sy:stationary-tensors} b=-H^f-p(dt\otimes w+w\otimes dt),\qquad \mathsf Q=K-b=C+p(dt\otimes w+w\otimes dt),\qquad s_p=p+\tfrac12.$$ Define the smooth scalar $$\label{sy:invariant-T} \mathcal T=\tfrac12\mathsf B(\mathsf Q,\mathsf Q) +\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}(w,\nabla t) +2s_p\|dt\|_{A_d}^2 +F\bigl(\operatorname{tr}C+2s_p w(t)\bigr).$$ This definition, rather than a choice of axis, fixes $\mathcal T$ also at zero slope.
- **Continuation system** ([source](#sy:homotopy)): For the continuation argument, let $$\label{sy:homotopy} (a,b)\in\mathcal H :=([0,1]\times\{1\})\cup(\{0\}\times[0,1]), \qquad K_a=aK, \qquad F_a=\eta f, \qquad \operatorname{div}V_a=b\,u\Xi_a.$$ Every expression containing $K$, including $F,V,\mathcal T,\tau$ and the constraint densities in scalar identities, is recomputed with $K_a$. The weights, $p,l,\eta$, $\delta_0$, and $C_N$ remain fixed. The original system is $(a,b)=(1,1)$; the two segments lead first to $(0,1)$ and then to $(0,0)$.
- **Polynomial parameter bounds** ([source](#pm-h-20)): We use $\mathcal P_N$ for a positive bound of the form $C(1+N)^a$, allowing the constant and the finite exponent to increase between appearances.
- **Active constraint rays** ([source](#va:active-rays)): Put $\alpha_1=*_{g}\mathcal E^\flat$ and $\alpha_2=*_{g}\mathcal B^\flat$. Use variations of $(g,K,\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ that are smooth and compactly supported, with support allowed to meet $B$; both form variations are closed. The unit ball is transported using the positive metric square root, so for $g'=h$ a transported vector has derivative $-\tfrac12h^\sharp v$. Let $$\label{va:active-rays} \mathcal A_B=\{(x,v):x\in\overline{\Omega_B},\ \|v\|_g\le1, \ \mu_m+J_m(v)=0\},\qquad \mathfrak C'=2(\mu_m+J_m(v))'.$$ Here $\Omega_B$ is the exterior to the chosen obstacle.
- **Multiplier complementarity** ([source](#va:complementarity)): Use the original obstacle from now on, and suppress its subscript. The scalar and vector first moments of $\Lambda$ define measures $u$ and $X$ relative to $dV_g$. Positivity and support on active rays mean, initially as measure statements, $$\label{va:complementarity} u\ge \|X\|_g,\qquad u\mu_m+J_m(X)=0.$$ Moment notation is used here because the measures will immediately be shown to have smooth densities.
- **Stationary original-data metric** ([source](#va:stationary-metric)): On $\mathbb R\times\operatorname{int}\Omega$ there are smooth stationary fields $$\label{va:stationary-metric} \mathbf G=-u^2dz^2+g_{ij}(dx^i+X^i dz)(dx^j+X^j dz), \qquad \xi=\partial_z,$$ and a two-form $\mathbf F$, with the prescribed orientation, which induce all four original data $(g,K,\mathcal E,\mathcal B)$ on each constant-$z$ slice. The Killing field is nonzero and future causal, and tends to the unit future timelike vector $(E/m,-P/m)$ relative to the original asymptotic normal and frame. Both Maxwell equations hold. With $\mathsf S$ as in Equation <a href="#va:maxwell-stress" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="va:maxwell-stress">[va:maxwell-stress]</a>, $$\begin{aligned} u(\mathbf{Ein}_{ij}-\mathsf S_{ij}) &=-(J_m)_{(i}X_{j)},\label{va:spatial-stress}\\ \mathbf{Ein}-\mathsf S &=\frac{\mu_m}{u^2}\,\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat. \label{va:null-stress} \end{aligned}$$ The coefficient is nonnegative; wherever it is positive, $\xi$ is null. In particular the region $W=-\mathbf G(\xi,\xi)=u^2-\|X\|_g^2>0$ is electrovacuum.
- **Reference slice with bifurcation boundary** ([source](#st:sigma-definition)): Let $$\label{st:sigma-definition} \Sigma=\{s_0=0\}\cup B_0\subset\widetilde{\mathfrak R}.$$ Near $B_0$ it is parametrized by $U=V=r\geq0$ and $y\in S$. It is therefore a smooth spacelike hypersurface with boundary $B_0$. It is closed: the local parametrization includes its only limits on the added faces, while escaping the asymptotically Euclidean end has no limit in the spacetime. It is connected and has a compact core and one Euclidean end. Its induced metric is complete with the boundary included.
- **Static orbit metric** ([source](#ri:orbit-metric)): On the open orbit space, the now positive function $W$ gives $$\label{ri:orbit-metric} g'=h_s=g+W^{-1}X_g^\flat\otimes X_g^\flat\geq g.$$ This is an equality of metrics after orbit projection in the interior; different boundary defining functions are allowed. The induced metric of $B_0$ equals the original metric on $TS$ by the attachment. Thus $\|B_0\|_{g'}=A$. The fixed set $B_0$ is totally geodesic in spacetime: its second fundamental vector is fixed by the differential of every Killing flow, while that differential acts as a nontrivial boost in the normal two-plane and has no fixed vector there. In particular $B_0$ is minimal in $g'$. The constraint and static equations give $$\label{ri:static-equations} R_{g'}=2\|\mathcal E'\|_{g'}^2,\qquad \operatorname{div}_{g'}\mathcal E'=0,\qquad \Delta_{g'}u'=\|\mathcal E'\|_{g'}^2u'.$$ For the last equation, the Ricci component in the future unit normal direction of a static metric is $(u')^{-1}\Delta_{g'}u'$. Electrovacuum has trace-free stress and that component of its Ricci tensor is $\|\mathcal E'\|^2$.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| q-adm-energy-charge-bound | ADM energy | ≥ | $\sqrt{\|P\|^2+Q^2}$ | The theorem also permits fixed future or past expansion signs chosen separately by boundary component. |
| q-invariant-mass-charge | Invariant ADM mass | ≥ | $Q$ | Total electric and magnetic charges enter through their magnitude. |
| q-enclosing-radius-upper-bound | Minimum-enclosing-area radius | ≤ | $m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$ | Disconnected boundary and arbitrary second fundamental form are permitted. |
| q-polynomial-upper-branch | Invariant ADM mass on the upper-radius branch | ≥ | $\frac12\left(r_A+\frac{Q^2}{r_A}\right)$ | The polynomial form is restricted to the radius strictly above the total charge magnitude. |
| q-positive-cut-area | Minimum full-cut area | > | $0$ | Nonempty compact smooth boundary and a single coordinate end. |
| q-polynomial-coercivity | Weighted sum of squared block variables | ≤ | $20(1+N)^2\mathcal T$ | The estimate loses only a polynomial factor in the filling parameter. |
| q-stationary-coercivity-lower | Stationary quadratic scalar | ≥ | $\tfrac12\mathcal E_0$ | The comparison is independent of the filling parameter. |
| q-distortion-scalar-upper | Divergence scalar | ≤ | $P_N$ | Prepared data and the floor parameter are fixed; the polynomial is independent of outer radius and homotopy parameters. |
| q-filled-mass-error | Nonnegative upper energy error | ≤ | $\mathcal P_N(\ell+\ell^{1/2})$ | The floor parameter remains fixed as the filling parameter tends to infinity. |
| q-flux-profile-energy-family | Prepared rest energy | ≥ | $sQ+\frac{1-s^2}{2}r_*$ | Profile and floor limits are taken in the stated order; endpoint estimates follow by limiting the profile parameter. |
| q-boundary-surface-gravity | Normalized surface gravity | = | $\frac c2$ | The Killing field is normalized by the original invariant ADM mass. |
| q-static-original-invariant-mass | Static orbit ADM energy | = | $m$ | Energy is evaluated in stationary rest coordinates. |
| q-sharp-example-area | Original minimum enclosing area of the sharp examples | = | $4\pi R_+^2$ | Actual outward fluxes are the prescribed signed charges. |
| q-boosted-energy | Actual ADM energy of a boosted equality example | = | $\gamma M$ | The boost is sufficiently small and the transition sufficiently distant to meet all admissibility conditions. |
| q-boosted-momentum | Actual ADM momentum of a boosted equality example | = | $\gamma Mv$ | The invariant mass remains the prescribed rest mass. |
